title: CEEMS: A Resource Manager Agnostic Energy and Emissions Monitoring Stack
problem: Users lack visibility into the energy consumption and emissions footprint of their ML/AI workloads across different resource managers and compute platforms. Rapid acceleration of ML/AI research has led to increased ICT energy consumption without adequate monitoring capabilities.
motivation: As ML/AI workloads consume significant energy, users must be aware of their applications' energy and emissions impact for sustainability and cost optimization.
method: CEEMS plugs into existing system-monitoring tools (Prometheus and Grafana, which track server activity) to collect energy-usage data from CPUs and graphics accelerators made by NVIDIA and AMD. It calculates the carbon emissions from that energy consumption. The system also lets data center operators write custom rules for how their hardware actually uses energy, and it works with any resource scheduler—whether on HPC systems or cloud platforms.
key_novelty: The core innovation is a system that measures energy and carbon emissions while working with any resource scheduler and any combination of CPU and GPU hardware.
contributions: Resource manager agnostic architecture for real-time energy and emissions monitoring across HPC and cloud platforms
Support for monitoring energy consumption on CPUs and NVIDIA/AMD GPU accelerators
Extensible design allowing data center operators to define custom energy estimation rules based on underlying hardware
Demonstrated deployment on large-scale HPC platform (Jean-Zay supercomputer with 1400+ nodes and 20k daily job churn)
primary_theme: Energy-aware workload monitoring and emissions tracking
